title: The Centre of the Earth Is as Hot as the Surface of the Sun

scenes.text: Right now, under your feet, it's as hot as the Sun's surface.
Earth's inner core is a ball of solid iron, more than five thousand kilometres down.
In twenty thirteen, French scientists crushed a speck of iron between two diamonds, to two million times normal air pressure, and heated it with lasers.
X-rays caught the exact moment it melted. The answer: about six thousand degrees Celsius.
That's a thousand degrees hotter than anyone thought, and about the same as the Sun's surface, which sits near five and a half thousand.
It's that hot because the planet is still cooling from the day it formed. And the iron only stays solid because of the crushing pressure on top of it.

description:
Right now, under your feet, it's as hot as the surface of the Sun.
In 2013, scientists at the ESRF synchrotron in Grenoble squeezed iron in a diamond anvil cell to more than two million atmospheres, heated it with lasers and used X-rays to see exactly when it melted. Extrapolated to the inner core boundary, the result was about 6,000 degrees Celsius, roughly 1,000 degrees hotter than earlier estimates and on par with the Sun's surface.
What else do you think is hiding under our feet?
